answer: Randomized admission by kernel delay. Each new identity must submit a registration proof; the system draws a random seed from a delayed beacon and assigns a wait slot derived from it. The agent's registration thread is admitted only after its slot, and the seed stays hidden until the commitment ridge is finalized, so attackers cannot precompute favorable slots or batch-register cheaply. Mass registration forces the attacker to pay full compute and idle time per identity with no scheduling advantage, collapsing the payoff of running many synthetic agents.
